response.sql: WITH hand_counts AS (SELECT p.throws AS hand, COUNT(DISTINCT ma.player_id) AS cnt FROM manager_award ma JOIN player p ON p.player_id = ma.player_id GROUP BY p.throws), shares AS (SELECT hand, cnt, cnt * 1.0 / SUM(cnt) OVER () AS share FROM hand_counts), avg_share AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share FROM shares), kept AS (SELECT s.cnt, s.share, a.avg_share FROM shares s CROSS JOIN avg_share a WHERE s.share > a.avg_share) SELECT SUM(cnt) AS total_count, AVG(share) AS avg_share, AVG(share - avg_share) AS avg_excess_over_average FROM kept;

assumptions.assumption: Unmatched awards are dropped by an inner join to the player table, and a missing throws value is a NULL, which GROUP BY keeps as its own group.
The average share across hands is the unweighted mean of the per-hand shares, computed over all hand groups before the filter is applied.
If the throws column stores blanks as empty strings rather than NULL, those would form a separate group, which this query does not merge with NULL.
